title: Retreats
hookLine: a few days away for silence and prayer
tomorrow: Block close: the house of prayer

lines: COME APART, AND REST A WHILE.
NO LEISURE SO MUCH AS TO EAT.
A GUEST HOUSE, A LAKE, A DRAWER.
cards: A weekend bag by the door, packed light. No laptop in it. Jesus once said to his tired friends, in Mark's Gospel: "Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while."
The next line: "for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat." Some Christians take that invitation literally. A weekend in the guest house of a monastery.
A few days at a retreat center by a lake. One day in a borrowed room, the phone left in a drawer, nothing on the schedule.

teach.b: First, Jesus did it himself. Mark says: "And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed."

Luke adds: "And he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed." And before he chooses the twelve, Luke says, he goes up a mountain and "continued all night in prayer to God." Second, the surprise.
Right after rest a while, they slip off by boat.

But the crowd sees them go, runs ahead on foot, and is waiting on the shore. Jesus steps out, and Mark says he "was moved with compassion toward them," and began to teach. The rest was real, and so was the interruption.
Third, how Christians go apart now.
Some monasteries keep guest rooms, and visitors join the monks at prayer, eat in silence, and walk.
Some retreats follow the Spiritual Exercises of Ignatius of Loyola, founder of the Jesuits, with a guide who meets you each day.
Some churches run weekend retreats with talks, singing and long walks; some people keep a single quiet day at home. The shape is the same: leave the noise on purpose, for a while, and then come back.

Last, the prophet Elijah, worn out and hiding in a cave, waits for God on a mountain. A great wind tears at the rocks, "but the LORD was not in the wind." Then an earthquake, then a fire, and God isn't in those either.
"And after the fire a still small voice." A voice that small is easy to miss in a wind. That's one reason people go on retreat at all.

how: Christians go on retreat at monastery guest houses, retreat centers and church weekends; some follow the Spiritual Exercises of Ignatius with a guide, and others keep a single quiet day of silence, prayer and walking.

o: going apart for a while for silence and prayer
leaving church for good after a hard season
a church's yearly business meeting and vote

p: after the wind, earthquake and fire

s: the Gospels never show Jesus taking time away
Mark and Luke both show him slipping off to solitary places to pray.
Elijah heard God in the great wind
"the LORD was not in the wind." after the fire came a still small voice.
in Luke, Jesus prayed all night before choosing the twelve
he "continued all night in prayer to God."

games.q: you're Jesus. you and your friends have finally slipped away by boat to rest. you step onto the shore, and a crowd has run ahead and is waiting. what do you do?
o: get back in the boat and find somewhere emptier.
send them home: you came here to rest.
have compassion on them, and begin to teach.
games.why: Mark says he "was moved with compassion toward them" and began to teach. the rest was real, and so was the interruption.

practice: Plan a quiet day now, a whole day, half a day or a single hour, and pick its date and place: a church, a park, your own kitchen with the phone put away.
Decide what you'll leave behind and what you'll bring, a Bible, a notebook, nothing at all. If you pray, offer that day to God now; if you don't, hold the date in mind and let it wait for you.

wordCard.voice: Retreats. Going apart on purpose, for a day or a few days, for silence and prayer, and then coming back.

orig.note: Greek: a lonely, empty place, the "desert place" Jesus calls his friends to in Mark 6:31.

carryVoice: Your line: come away awhile. Even Jesus went apart, and then came back. See you soon.
